from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the 'Shrinking' Interval", [
            "Two points define a secant line.",
            "As the points get closer, the gap shrinks.",
            "The secant line tilts as the gap closes.",
            "At the limit, it touches one point.",
            "This is the tangent line."
        ])

        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, color=BLUE)
        graph = VGroup(axes, curve)
        self.place_in_area(graph, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        a_val = 2.0
        h = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        point_a = Dot(axes.c2p(a_val, 0.5 * a_val**2), color=YELLOW)
        point_b = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(axes.c2p(a_val + h.get_value(), 0.5 * (a_val + h.get_value())**2), color=RED))
        
        def get_secant():
            p1 = axes.c2p(a_val, 0.5 * a_val**2)
            p2 = axes.c2p(a_val + h.get_value(), 0.5 * (a_val + h.get_value())**2)
            return Line(p1, p2, color=GREEN)
            
        secant = always_redraw(get_secant)
        
        self.add(graph, point_a, point_b, secant)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(h.animate.set_value(0.1), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(h.animate.set_value(0.05), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(h.animate.set_value(0.01), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We define the slope as a limit.",
            "The formula uses a difference quotient.",
            "As h approaches zero, we get the derivative.",
            "It maps the slope at any input x.",
            "The derivative gives the instantaneous rate."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Derivative", lecture_lines)
        
        # Formula setup
        # f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}
        formula = MathTex(
            "f'(x) = \\lim_{h \\to 0} \\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}",
            font_size=40
        )
        
        # Define colored parts for specific components
        # f(x+h) is part 2, f(x) is part 4
        formula.set_color_by_tex("f(x+h)", YELLOW)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("f(x)", BLUE)
        
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'D5')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(formula), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        # Highlight components
        self.play(Indicate(formula[0][10:])) # The quotient part
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Indicate(formula[0][5:10])) # The limit notation
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Indicate(formula[0][0:4])) # f'(x)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color(RED))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Velocity is the derivative of position.",
            "Our robot moves at f of t equals t squared.",
            "At three seconds, the derivative is six.",
            "So velocity is six units per second.",
            "Calculus measures real-world motion precisely."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: Real-time Velocity", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 10, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        graph = axes.plot(lambda t: t**2, color=BLUE)
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(3, 9), color=YELLOW)
        slope_line = TangentLine(graph, alpha=0.75, length=2, color=RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(axes, graph), 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(point))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.play(Create(slope_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        label = MathTex("v(3) = 6").next_to(point, UP)
        self.play(Write(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PURPLE)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[4]))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["We traveled from average to instantaneous.", "The derivative acts as a mathematical zoom.", "It gives us precision at a single point."]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Summary", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visuals
        # recap_text: Recap: Secant (Average) -> Tangent (Instantaneous)
        recap_text = Text("Secant (Avg) \u2192 Tangent (Inst.)", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        
        # zoom_lens: Simple circle/shape representation for zoom
        zoom_lens = Circle(radius=1.0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        zoom_text = Text("Zoom", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).next_to(zoom_lens, DOWN)
        zoom_group = VGroup(zoom_lens, zoom_text)
        
        # derivative_formula: MathTex for final derivative
        deriv_formula = MathTex(r"f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}", font_size=36, color=GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(recap_text, 'B2', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(recap_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(zoom_group, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(zoom_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(deriv_formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(deriv_formula))
        
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Introduction: From Average to Instantaneous
sections.content: Define 'Average Rate of Change' using the slope of a secant line. Transition to the challenge: What if we want to know the speed at a single, exact moment? Introduce a sprinter (the Cheetah) running a race.
sections.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed = 20 m/s. But how fast was it moving at exactly 2.5 seconds?

sections.title: Visualizing the 'Shrinking' Interval
sections.content: Use a graphical animation showing two points on a curve getting closer together. As the distance between points (Δx) approaches zero, the secant line transforms into a tangent line.
sections.example: Visualize the secant line segment connecting t=2 and t=3 on a position-time graph, then shrinking the gap until it touches only at t=2.5.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Introduce the mathematical formalization: the limit of the difference quotient. Define the derivative as the slope of the tangent line at any point x.
sections.example: Formula: f'(x) = lim (h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Represent this as the slope (m) of the tangent line at a specific point.

sections.title: Application: Real-time Velocity
sections.content: Connect the abstract derivative back to the physical world. Explain that velocity is the derivative of position with respect to time.
sections.example: A robot arm's movement path follows f(t) = t². Use the derivative to show the robot's exact velocity at t=3 seconds is 6 units/sec.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
sections.content: Summarize that the derivative is the 'mathematical zoom lens' that allows us to find the rate of change at a single point, enabling precision in engineering and science.
sections.example: Recap: Secant line (Average) → Tangent line (Instantaneous) → Derivative (The tool for precision).
